title: POC constraints and airgap deploy options
body:
Executive summary:

This note captures feasibility findings, recommended deployment patterns, and an itemized constraints matrix for the upcoming on-prem/air-gapped POC. Goal is to produce a minimal-risk POC that validates our serving runtime (small model profile and a medium model profile), the private control plane connectivity model, and offline image/patch workflows.

POC objectives:
- Validate end-to-end inference: local client -> private API -> model runtime -> response under 200ms p50 for short prompts (8-16 tokens generation) in dedicated single-GPU nodes.
- Demonstrate airgap-safe image distribution, signature verification, and offline patch flow.
- Integrate with customer KMS/HSM for keywrap and envelope encryption of model artifacts and token store.
- Prove observability: metrics, tracing, and audit logs exported to customer SIEM in offline-friendly ways.

Constraints/assumptions collected during pre-workshop: 
- Customer environment: locked-down datacenter with no egress; internal dev VLAN and production VLAN separated by firewall.
- Allowed media: signed USB or customer-controlled internal registry via import node. No external internet access from production cluster.
- Preferred orchestrator: upstream Kubernetes 1.27 (customer-run), with containerd as runtime.
- GPUs: mixture of NVIDIA A10/A100; customer can allocate 1–4 GPUs for POC.
- Security/compliance: FIPS 140-2 HSM for KMS preferred; SOC 2-related audit logging required.

Deployment options evaluated (high level):
1) Offline image bundle + airgap registry import
   - Produce a tarball of images + Helm charts + SBOM + detached signatures. Customer uses a bastion/import node to push to internal registry.
   - Pros: Standard, reusable; easy to script.
   - Cons: Requires import node, careful registry compatibility checks.
2) Signed image set + local OCI mirror (registryless runtime via imgpkg)
   - Use tools to unpack OCI layout directly to nodes or to a local OCI filesystem. Good for environments that forbid registries.
   - Pros: No registry dependency.
   - Cons: More manual, less familiar for k8s operators.
3) Operator + controller installed from bundle, then pull from internal registry
   - Deploy Redwood operator and CRs from the offline bundle; operator handles node-level model lifecycle.
   - Pros: Better long-term manageability.
   - Cons: Adds operator testing surface for POC.

Security controls and artifact integrity:
- All images in bundle will be signed using sigstore/cosign with a detached signature. We will provide a small verification shim that runs in initContainers to validate images before starting pods.
- Provide SBOMs (CycloneDX) for every image and a short policy doc for customers to review components.
- Model artifacts (weights) will be encrypted with envelope encryption; root KEK will be stored in customer HSM or Vault namespace. We will provide a sample HashiCorp Vault integration using transit with mTLS.

KMS/HSM integration notes:
- Preferred flow: Redwood encrypts model keys with a symmetric data key that the customer KMS wraps with an HSM-managed KEK.
- Options: HashiCorp Vault (transit), AWS CloudHSM (if connected via customer VPC), or Thales Luna for full FIPS chain.
- Required customer artifacts: KMS endpoint, certs for mTLS, service account with wrap/unwrap permissions.

Network & firewall requirements (POC minimal set):
- Internal registry (if chosen): 10.10.20.5:5000 (example) allow on prod-k8s nodes from import-bastion.
- Control plane (private): 10.10.30.0/24 nodes must reach each other on etcd and k8s API ports.
- Bastion/import node egress: allowed to local mirror host only; no internet.
- Monitoring collector: allow outbound from collector node to SIEM ingest endpoint (if customer provides connection). If no outbound is allowed, we will show how to export periodic bundles to a staging host.
- Sample firewall rules for POC (customer network team to validate):
  - Allow TCP 5000 from import-bastion -> internal-registry
  - Allow TCP 2379/2380 between control-plane nodes
  - Allow kubelet (10250) from admin jump host

Host OS, drivers, and runtime requirements:
- CentOS 8 Stream or Ubuntu 22.04 LTS are validated platforms; kernel >=5.15 strongly recommended.
- NVIDIA driver: matching supported CUDA: for A10/A100 use NVIDIA driver 530.x / CUDA 11.8 compatibility. We will provide a GPU driver verification checklist.
- Container runtime: containerd v1.7+ or Docker Engine 24.x (containerd preferred).
- Storage: model weights store on local SSDs with at least 1TB free for medium model profile; provision NFS for shared cache if required.

Offline patching and updates approach:
- Monthly patch bundle: signed tarball containing images, helm charts, operator manifests, SBOM and patch notes.
- Customer will import to import-bastion which pushes to internal registry or drops to internal OCI mirror.
- Provide a lightweight upgrade-runner job (stateless container) that runs in customer admin namespace and validates images by signature, checks SBOM, performs canary rollout using Kubernetes labels.

Observability in airgap:
- Metrics: expose Prometheus endpoints; for airgap we recommend a local Prometheus + Grafana on customer cluster. We will provide Grafana dashboards packaged in the bundle.
- Tracing: Zipkin/Jaeger local collector optional.
- Logs: Fluent Bit/Fluentd to forward to customer ELK/SIEM; if outbound is blocked, show archive-and-transfer pattern with daily zipped logs pushed from admin host.
- Audit: Kubernetes audit policy needed. Redwood components will emit structured JSON audit events to stdout and a local audit sink.

Acceptance criteria for POC (must be measurable):
- Functional: Successful completion of 100 inference requests for small and medium models with correct outputs under test harness.
- Performance: p50 latency <= 200ms for small model profile; p95 <= 350ms under 5 RPS sustained.
- Security: All runtime images verify via cosign and SBOMs are consumable by customer review team. KMS wrap/unwrap flows complete with HSM and keys are not persisted in plaintext.
- Operability: Team can perform a full offline image import and a coordinated canary rollout without vendor remote access.

Minimum test plan (deliverables):
- Lightweight test harness (go binary + curl script) to run against internal endpoint with canned prompts and assert outputs.
- Load script (k6 or wrk) with predefined token/headers.
- Artifact: step-by-step import document for network + admin teams.

Resource estimate for a 2-week POC (rough):
- HW: 1 control-plane (3 masters recommended but single allowed for POC), 2 worker nodes with 1 GPU each (A10), 1 admin/import bastion.
- People: 0.4 FTE solutions engineer (setup), 0.2 FTE infra engineer (customer side), 0.1 FTE security reviewer.
- Time: 5 business days for install + 3 days tuning + 3 days test/acceptance + buffer.

Action items & owners (initial):
- Provide offline bundle spec (images, charts, SBOM format) -> Leah Park (ETA 2026-03-05)
- Customer to confirm allowed import methods (USB vs import-bastion) and provide registry hostname -> Owen Li (customer contact) (ETA 2026-02-20)
- Vault/HSM integration runbook draft -> Priya Shah (ETA 2026-02-28)
- Prepare dashboard package and Grafana JSON -> Mateo Alvarez (ETA 2026-03-01)

Open questions / risks:
- Risk: Customer internal registry uses non-standard auth (LDAP-based) that our import tooling must support. Mitigation: build a simple registry adapter script and test in lab.
- Question: Can we get a short-lived admin VM with outbound to a staging AWS account for faster image import for the first run? If not, additional manual steps will be required.
- Risk: HSM latency causing wrap/unwrap to exceed SLO. Mitigation: cache unwrapped data keys in memory with TTL; measure during POC.

Appendix: quick verification checklist (POC day-of):
- Check kernel/driver: nvidia-smi shows expected GPUs; docker/containerd can run nvidia-container-runtime.
- Verify signature: cosign verify --key <pubkey> <image.tar.gz.sig>
- Verify SBOM presence: sbom-cyclonedx.json exists next to each image.
- Run sample inference: ./poc-harness --endpoint https://internal-redwood:8443 --prompts ./prompts/smoke.json

Notes for internal team: this doc should be treated as a conversation starter with the customer network/security teams. The final POC scope will be adjusted based on their import constraints and HSM availability. Keep the first run as minimal as possible to reduce unknowns.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-04 created initial draft after discovery workshop.
- 2025-12-12 added KMS/HSM integration pattern and offline patching plan.
- 2026-02-28 updated acceptance criteria and action owners after customer call.
